title: Sheinbaum Says Amnesty International “Is Co-opted” and Against the Government of Mexico
author: Arturo Sánchez and Alonso Urrutia
content:
_This article by Arturo Sánchez and Alonso Urrutia originally appeared in
the[October 27, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/27/politica/sheinbaum-
asegura-que-amnistia-internacional-esta-cooptada-y-en-contra-de-mexico),
Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City**. Amnesty International **" is co-opted"** and against the
government of Mexico, charged President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, who stated
that the organization intends to organize events in the country after "the
work" of her administration on the disappearance of persons "was recognized"
at the United Nations (UN).

Asked at her morning press conference in the National Palace about the stance
of the UN General Assembly, where no member state pushed for actions against
Mexico following the report of the Committee on Enforced Disappearances (CED),
the president recalled that the government rejected that document because it
attributed to the State enforced disappearances that, she maintained,
"occurred during the dirty war."

> Today we have problems of disappearance, mainly linked to organized crime or
> crimes, and the victims and their families are being attended to. So, that
> view seemed very biased to us.
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum

She highlighted that the Secretariat of Foreign Affairs (SRE) and the
Undersecretariat of Human Rights of the Secretariat of Governance (SG)
presented to the UN last week the legal reforms that were approved and the
location of **more than 16,000 people**.

According to Sheinbaum Pardo, Amnesty International seeks to hold other events
in Mexico because "they saw that the work we are doing was recognized," which
is why the SG held a press conference yesterday.

She announced that starting this Wednesday, the meetings of the SG, the Office
of the Attorney General of the Republic, the National Search Commission, the
Executive Commission for Victim Assistance and the state governments with
collectives of searching mothers will resume, in what she described as **" a
permanent dialogue."**
